_doc: Task A protocol, declared BEFORE any ablation inference. Existing v3 checkpoints only (no retraining).

fixed.language: Pick up the Pringles can with the right arm, hand it to the left arm
fixed.noise: one N(0,1) tensor (50 x 32) per (episode, frame), from numpy seed 20261105 + 1000*episode + frame, identical for every checkpoint and condition
fixed.autocast: bf16 inference autocast for every run
fixed.preprocessing: the checkpoint's own saved pre/post processors

conditions.wrong_episode: frame of the held-out episode whose initial lid click is farthest from this episode's, at the same relative time (nearest sampled frame)
conditions.object_occluded: pixels of the Pringles can replaced by mid-grey: disk around the Gate-1 HSV lid track (radius max(45 px, 1.4 x equivalent lid radius)) plus HSV-red pixels within 150 px of the lid, dilated 9 px; last known lid position when the tracker is lost
conditions.state_only: image tokens removed from attention via observation.images.camera1_padding_mask = False (diagnostic)

phases_per_step: each chunk step is labelled by the phase of its OWN target frame t+k: approach [0, rc-5), grasp [rc-5, rc+15), carry [rc+15, lc-5), handover [lc-5, ro+5), release [ro+5, T) from the held-out episode's gripper commands
normalisation: per-joint action std of the TRAINING real source episodes (real_10 episodes 0-9), not of held-out data

near_far.rule: distance (body_cam px) of the held-out episode's human-clicked initial lid to the nearest source-episode (0-9) initial click; near <= 40 px, far > 40 px
near_far.secondary: far episodes within 20 px of an exported v3 C relocated initial lid position are additionally marked 'far_covered_by_generation'

reporting: per-step phase-balanced error, per phase, gripper transition timing, |prediction(intervention) - prediction(original)|, grouped by held-out recording with recording-level bootstrap (2000 resamples); original v3 start-frame metric also reported
interpretation_rule: image dependence is called CLEAR for an arm only if blank AND wrong_episode both raise its primary phase-balanced error by >= 10% relative and the recording-level 95% CI of the increase excludes 0; a small effect of one OOD intervention alone is not evidence that vision is ignored
